title: Motion to Suppress Evidence with Incorporated Police Report Narrative
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF HARRIS COUNTY, TEXAS
340TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. 2024-56789-H

STATE OF TEXAS, Plaintiff
v.
MARIA O’NEIL, Defendant

MOTION TO SUPPRESS EVIDENCE

COMES NOW, Maria O’Neil, Defendant in the above-entitled and numbered cause, by and through her undersigned counsel, and respectfully moves this Honorable Court to suppress all evidence obtained as a result of the warrantless search of her vehicle on March 15, 2024. In support thereof, Defendant incorporates the narrative of Houston Police Department Officer James T. Kowalski, as set forth in the police report attached hereto as Exhibit A, and states as follows:

1. On March 15, 2024, at approximately 11:45 p.m., Officer Kowalski observed a dark-colored sedan bearing Texas license plate GVT-8421 traveling northbound on Interstate 45 near the intersection of West Road. The vehicle displayed a cracked taillight, which Officer Kowalski believed constituted a traffic violation under Texas Transportation Code § 547.322.

2. Officer Kowalski initiated a traffic stop at the 6100 block of North Freeway. The vehicle pulled into a well-lit gas station at 6220 North Freeway, Houston, Texas 77022. The driver was later identified as Maria O’Neil, date of birth: 08/14/1989.

3. Upon approaching the vehicle, Officer Kowalski states: “I observed a strong odor of burnt marijuana emanating from the passenger compartment. I asked the driver for her license and insurance. She appeared nervous and avoided eye contact.” [1]

4. Officer Kowalski then requested backup. Officer Sarah J. Langford arrived at the scene at approximately 11:52 p.m. Officer Langford conducted a records check and discovered that the vehicle’s registered owner, one exhibitJohn Doe, had an outstanding warrant for parole violation.

5. The police report narrative continues: “I asked [O’Neil] to step out of the vehicle. She complied. I then searched the vehicle incident to arrest. Under the front passenger seat, I discovered a black zippered pouch containing a white crystalline substance later field-tested positive for methamphetamine, weighing approximately 28.3 grams.” [2]

6. Officer Kowalski further states: “I also located a digital scale with residue, several small plastic baggies, and a firearm, a Taurus G2C 9mm, serial number TAU-98765-ABC, under the driver’s seat. The firearm was loaded with nine rounds of ammunition.”

7. The Defendant contends that the search was not incident to a valid arrest because the traffic stop was pretextual and lacked reasonable suspicion for the search. The alleged odor of marijuana is insufficient to support a warrantless search under the Texas Constitution. See, e.g., State v. Martinez, 567 S.W.3d 789 (Tex. Crim. App. 2019); but see also Rodriguez v. United States, 575 U.S. 348 (2015).

8. The police report further notes that the vehicle bore VIN 1HGCM82633A004792 and was insured under policy number POL-7748392-01 issued by Lone Star Insurance Group, an organization with offices in Austin, Texas. The insurance card listed the named insured as “John-David O’Neil,” a hyphenated surname variant.

9. Officer Kowalski’s bar number is 47821, and he has been with HPD for 12 years. The case file is Bates-stamped HPD-2024-0315-0001 through HPD-2024-0315-0045.

10. The Defendant further notes that the search violated the Fourth Amendment as interpreted by the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals. See, e.g., State v. Granville, 423 S.W.3d 399 (Tex. Crim. App. 2014). The evidence must be suppressed as fruit of the poisonous tree.

11. The Defendant’s counsel, Michael R. Thornton, State Bar Number 24056789, of the law firm Thornton & Associates, PLLC, located at 1200 Main Street, Suite 400, Houston, Texas 77002, requests an evidentiary hearing on this motion.

12. The Defendant’s address is 4523 Elmcroft Drive, Houston, Texas 77084. Her phone number is (713) 555-0198 and her email address is maria.o’neil@email.com. Her Social Security Number is 456-78-9123.

WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, Defendant Maria O’Neil respectfully requests that this Court grant this Motion to Suppress and enter an order suppressing all evidence obtained as a result of the illegal search.

Respectfully submitted,

__________________________
Michael R. Thornton
Attorney for Defendant
State Bar No. 24056789

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I hereby certify that a true and correct copy of the foregoing Motion was served upon the Harris County District Attorney’s Office, 1201 Franklin Street, Houston, Texas 77002, on this 10th day of April, 2024.

__________________________
Michael R. Thornton

FOOTNOTES

[1] Officer Kowalski’s exact words as recorded in the police report narrative, page 3, lines 12-14.
[2] Id. at page 4, lines 1-5.
public_law: State v. Martinez, 567 S.W.3d 789 (Tex. Crim. App. 2019)
State v. Granville, 423 S.W.3d 399 (Tex. Crim. App. 2014)

title: Motion to Quash Indictment with Police Report Narrative
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF DALLAS COUNTY, TEXAS
195TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. DC-24-09876

STATE OF TEXAS, Plaintiff
v.
ROBERT JENKINS-SMITH, Defendant

MOTION TO QUASH INDICTMENT

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, Robert Jenkins-Smith, Defendant in the above-styled and numbered cause, by and through his attorney of record, and moves the Court to quash the indictment returned against him on February 14, 2024. This motion is based on the police report narrative of Detective Angela M. Vasquez, attached as Exhibit B, and the following points and authorities:

1. The indictment fails to allege an essential element of the offense of theft under Texas Penal Code § 31.03, specifically that the property was taken without the effective consent of the owner.

2. The police report narrative states: “On January 22, 2024, at approximately 3:30 p.m., I was dispatched to 7890 Commerce Drive, Dallas, Texas 75201, in reference to a theft at a construction site. Upon arrival, I met with the complainant, Mr. Harold Finch, site supervisor for BuildRight Contractors, Inc.” [1]

3. The narrative continues: “Mr. Finch stated that he observed the suspect, later identified as Robert Jenkins-Smith, loading copper wiring into a white Ford F-150 with Texas license plate ABC-1234. Mr. Finch confronted the suspect, who stated, ‘I have permission from [Smith] to take this material.’” The editorial brackets appear in the original report.

4. Detective Vasquez’s bar number is 58321. She has been with the Dallas Police Department for 15 years. The case file is Bates-stamped DPD-2024-0122-0001 through DPD-2024-0122-0032.

5. The defendant’s vehicle bore VIN 1FTFW1EF7EKF12345 and was insured under policy number AUTO-998877-66 issued by Texas Premier Insurance, an organization headquartered in Dallas, Texas.

6. The police report notes that the defendant’s date of birth is June 17, 1985, and his Social Security Number is 987-65-4321. His phone number is (214) 555-0147 and his email address is r.jenkins-smith@workmail.com.

7. The defendant’s counsel, Patricia L. O’Malley, State Bar Number 34567890, of the firm O’Malley & Associates, PLLC, located at 500 North Akard Street, Suite 200, Dallas, Texas 75201, argues that the indictment is defective because it does not specify the manner or means of the theft.

8. The police report further indicates that the complainant, Harold Finch, provided a written statement. Finch is not a party to this action but is a witness for the State.

9. The State relies on the case of State v. Thompson, 456 S.W.3d 234 (Tex. App.—Dallas 2015, pet. ref’d), but the Defendant distinguishes that case because the indictment there contained specific factual allegations lacking here.

10. The Defendant also cites Ex parte Johnson, 589 S.W.3d 876 (Tex. Crim. App. 2019), in support of the proposition that an indictment must give the defendant sufficient notice.

11. The undersigned counsel certifies that a copy of this motion was served on the Dallas County District Attorney’s Office, 133 N. Riverfront Blvd, Dallas, Texas 75207, on March 1, 2024.

WHEREFORE, Defendant Robert Jenkins-Smith prays that this Court quash the indictment and dismiss the case.

Respectfully submitted,

__________________________
Patricia L. O’Malley
Attorney for Defendant
State Bar No. 34567890

FOOTNOTES

[1] Police report narrative, page 2, lines 8-12.
[2] Id. at page 3, lines 3-5.
public_law: State v. Thompson, 456 S.W.3d 234 (Tex. App.—Dallas 2015, pet. ref’d)
Ex parte Johnson, 589 S.W.3d 876 (Tex. Crim. App. 2019)

title: Motion for Discovery with Police Report Narrative
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF BEXAR COUNTY, TEXAS
144TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. 2024-CR-12345

STATE OF TEXAS, Plaintiff
v.
CARLOS GARCIA-RAMIREZ, Defendant

MOTION FOR DISCOVERY

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

NOW COMES, Carlos Garcia-Ramirez, Defendant in the above-entitled cause, by and through his undersigned counsel, and respectfully requests that this Court order the State to produce certain discovery pursuant to Texas Code of Criminal Procedure art. 39.14. In support thereof, Defendant incorporates the police report narrative of San Antonio Police Officer Kevin M. O’Brien, attached as Exhibit C, and states:

1. On February 28, 2024, at approximately 2:15 a.m., Officer O’Brien was on patrol in the 300 block of South Flores Street, San Antonio, Texas 78204, when he observed a silver Honda Accord with Texas license plate LMR-6655 fail to stop at a red light.

2. Officer O’Brien initiated a traffic stop at the intersection of South Flores and Durango Boulevard. The driver was identified as Carlos Garcia-Ramirez, date of birth: November 3, 1992.

3. The police report narrative states: “Upon approaching the vehicle, I detected a strong odor of alcohol on the driver’s breath. I asked the driver to step out and perform field sobriety tests. The driver complied.” [1]

4. The narrative continues: “During the field sobriety tests, the driver exhibited multiple clues of intoxication. I placed him under arrest for DWI. A subsequent search of the vehicle incident to arrest revealed an open container of beer in the center console.” [2]

5. Officer O’Brien’s bar number is 61234. The case file is Bates-stamped SAPD-2024-0228-0001 through SAPD-2024-0228-0020.

6. The defendant’s vehicle bore VIN 1HGCG1659WA029847 and was insured under policy number DWI-INS-45678-02 issued by Alamo Insurance Group, an organization with offices in San Antonio, Texas.

7. The defendant’s Social Security Number is 234-56-7890. His phone number is (210) 555-0321 and his email address is c.garcia-ramirez@fastmail.com.

8. The defendant’s counsel, David A. Kowalski, State Bar Number 45678901, of the firm Kowalski & Lee, PLLC, located at 1010 Navarro Street, Suite 300, San Antonio, Texas 78205, seeks disclosure of all audio and video recordings of the stop, as well as the results of any chemical testing.

9. The State relies on the case of State v. Martinez, 678 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. App.—San Antonio 2023, no pet.), but the Defendant notes that case is distinguishable because there the officer had a warrant.

10. The Defendant also cites Fowkes v. State, 543 S.W.3d 789 (Tex. Crim. App. 2018), for the proposition that the State must preserve exculpatory evidence.

11. Undersigned counsel certifies service on the Bexar County District Attorney’s Office, 300 Dolorosa Street, San Antonio, Texas 78205, on March 10, 2024.

WHEREFORE, Defendant Carlos Garcia-Ramirez prays that this Court grant this Motion for Discovery and order the State to produce the requested materials.

Respectfully submitted,

__________________________
David A. Kowalski
Attorney for Defendant
State Bar No. 45678901

FOOTNOTES

[1] Police report narrative, page 1, lines 15-18.
[2] Id. at page 2, lines 1-4.
public_law: Texas Code of Criminal Procedure art. 39.14
State v. Martinez, 678 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. App.—San Antonio 2023, no pet.)
Fowkes v. State, 543 S.W.3d 789 (Tex. Crim. App. 2018)

title: Motion for New Trial with Police Report Narrative
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF TARRANT COUNTY, TEXAS
432ND JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. 2023-87654-T

STATE OF TEXAS, Plaintiff
v.
AMANDA L. HARTWELL, Defendant

MOTION FOR NEW TRIAL

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, Amanda L. Hartwell, Defendant in the above-captioned cause, by and through her undersigned counsel, and moves the Court to grant a new trial based on newly discovered evidence and ineffective assistance of counsel. In support thereof, Defendant incorporates the police report narrative of Fort Worth Police Officer Derek J. Simmons, attached as Exhibit D, and states:

1. On October 12, 2023, at approximately 10:00 p.m., Officer Simmons was dispatched to 2200 West 7th Street, Fort Worth, Texas 76107, in reference to a disturbance at a bar called The Rusty Nail.

2. The police report narrative states: “Upon arrival, I observed a female subject, later identified as Amanda L. Hartwell, arguing with another female subject. I attempted to intervene, but the defendant pushed me. I placed her under arrest for assault on a peace officer.” [1]

3. The narrative continues: “During a pat-down search incident to arrest, I located a small plastic bag containing a white powdery substance in the defendant’s left front pants pocket. The substance field-tested positive for cocaine.” [2]

4. Officer Simmons’s bar number is 72456. The case file is Bates-stamped FWPD-2023-1012-0001 through FWPD-2023-1012-0025.

5. The defendant’s vehicle, a blue Ford Explorer with VIN 1FM5K8D81FGA12345, was impounded. The vehicle was insured under policy number FW-INS-56789-03 issued by Cowtown Insurance Agency, an organization based in Fort Worth, Texas.

6. The defendant’s date of birth is April 22, 1990, and her Social Security Number is 345-67-8901. Her phone number is (817) 555-0284 and her email address is amanda.hartwell@cablemail.com.

7. The defendant’s trial counsel, Steven M. O’Connor, State Bar Number 56789012, of the firm O’Connor & Associates, PLLC, located at 500 Throckmorton Street, Suite 100, Fort Worth, Texas 76102, failed to call a material witness, one exhibitJohn Smith, who would have testified that the defendant did not push the officer.

8. The State relied on the case of State v. Brown, 789 S.W.3d 654 (Tex. Crim. App. 2021), but the Defendant notes that case involved a different factual scenario.

9. The Defendant also cites Ex parte Martinez, 456 S.W.3d 321 (Tex. Crim. App. 2015), for the proposition that ineffective assistance of counsel warrants a new trial.

10. Undersigned counsel certifies service on the Tarrant County District Attorney’s Office, 401 W. Belknap Street, Fort Worth, Texas 76196, on March 20, 2024.

WHEREFORE, Defendant Amanda L. Hartwell prays that this Court grant a new trial.

Respectfully submitted,

__________________________
Steven M. O’Connor
Attorney for Defendant
State Bar No. 56789012

FOOTNOTES

[1] Police report narrative, page 1, lines 10-14.
[2] Id. at page 2, lines 1-4.
public_law: State v. Brown, 789 S.W.3d 654 (Tex. Crim. App. 2021)
Ex parte Martinez, 456 S.W.3d 321 (Tex. Crim. App. 2015)

title: Motion in Limine with Police Report Narrative
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF TRAVIS COUNTY, TEXAS
427TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. D-1-DC-24-000567

STATE OF TEXAS, Plaintiff
v.
JONATHAN R. WHITAKER, Defendant

MOTION IN LIMINE

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

NOW COMES, Jonathan R. Whitaker, Defendant in the above-numbered cause, by and through his undersigned counsel, and respectfully requests that this Court enter an order in limine prohibiting the State from introducing certain evidence at trial. In support thereof, Defendant incorporates the police report narrative of Austin Police Officer Lisa M. Chen, attached as Exhibit E, and states:

1. On December 5, 2023, at approximately 8:30 p.m., Officer Chen was dispatched to 1200 East 6th Street, Austin, Texas 78702, in reference to a reported theft at a convenience store.

2. The police report narrative states: “Upon arrival, I was met by the store clerk, Mr. Kevin O’Neil, who stated that the suspect, later identified as Jonathan R. Whitaker, had taken several items without paying. Mr. O’Neil provided a description and pointed to the suspect walking east on 6th Street.” [1]

3. The narrative continues: “I detained the suspect and conducted a pat-down search. During the search, I felt a hard object in the suspect’s jacket pocket. I removed the object, which was a small digital scale with residue. I then placed the suspect under arrest for theft.” [2]

4. Officer Chen’s bar number is 83456. The case file is Bates-stamped APD-2023-1205-0001 through APD-2023-1205-0018.

5. The defendant’s vehicle, a black Chevrolet Malibu with VIN 1G1ZD5ST3LF123456, was parked nearby. The vehicle was insured under policy number AUS-INS-23456-04 issued by Capital City Insurance, an organization with offices in Austin, Texas.

6. The defendant’s date of birth is July 14, 1987, and his Social Security Number is 567-89-0123. His phone number is (512) 555-0462 and his email address is j.r.whitaker@freemail.com.

7. The defendant’s counsel, Rachel M. O’Donnell, State Bar Number 67890123, of the firm O’Donnell & Harper, PLLC, located at 100 Congress Avenue, Suite 200, Austin, Texas 78701, moves to exclude any reference to the defendant’s prior arrests, as such evidence is more prejudicial than probative.

8. The State relies on the case of State v. Davis, 654 S.W.3d 567 (Tex. App.—Austin 2022, pet. granted), but the Defendant notes that case is not final.

9. The Defendant also cites Hernandez v. State, 432 S.W.3d 890 (Tex. Crim. App. 2014), in support of the motion.

10. Undersigned counsel certifies service on the Travis County District Attorney’s Office, 509 W. 11th Street, Austin, Texas 78701, on April 1, 2024.

WHEREFORE, Defendant Jonathan R. Whitaker prays that this Court grant this Motion in Limine.

Respectfully submitted,

__________________________
Rachel M. O’Donnell
Attorney for Defendant
State Bar No. 67890123

FOOTNOTES

[1] Police report narrative, page 1, lines 8-12.
[2] Id. at page 2, lines 1-4.
public_law: State v. Davis, 654 S.W.3d 567 (Tex. App.—Austin 2022, pet. granted)
Hernandez v. State, 432 S.W.3d 890 (Tex. Crim. App. 2014)
